reason: E1 directly supports that Cr, Ni, Mn segregate and form embrittling nanoclusters at GBs in this alloy system, and that this occurs at intermediate temperatures. However, E1 provides no evidence that tailored heat treatments (600–900°C holds) can control or reverse this clustering to preserve toughness; that premise is entirely unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Cr, Ni, and Mn segregate to grain boundaries in CrMnFeCoNi HEAs
This segregation forms nanoclusters at grain boundaries
These nanoclusters reduce grain boundary cohesion and cause embrittlement
The segregation and embrittlement occur at intermediate temperatures (<700°C)
Controlling nanoclustering via heat treatment can preserve toughness
